newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian government bans anti-logging march.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian government bans anti-logging march.

text.p: The Cambodian government has banned a planned opposition march against rampant deforestation, reversing an earlier decision to allow the demonstration, the unrecognised Khmer Nation Party (KNP) said on Friday.
But defiant KNP leader Sam Rainsy told Reuters the party would go ahead with the demonstration.
"We will make a surprise move. We are not going to confine ourselves in our headquarters," he said.
The KNP had moved the date of the March to Sunday November 3 after an earlier government objection.
The government does not recognise the KNP, whose leader was sacked as finance minister in 1994 and expelled from parliament in 1995.
Rainsy has been fierce in his attacks on government forestry policies and alleged high-level corruption in connection with deals that leave the country's dwindling forest cover.
The KNP's concerns about logging and forestry policies are shared by King Norodom Sihanouk, donor nations, major lending institutions and environmentalists.
